chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ahmad ibn Ismail the scribe, from his father, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was in the Sacred Mosque, and a group from the Quraysh looked at him and said, 'Who is this?' It was said to them, 'The Imam of the people of Iraq.' Some of them said, 'Send one of you to him to ask him.' So a young man from them came to him and said to him, 'O cousin, what is the greatest of the major sins?' He said: 'Drinking wine.'

He went to them and informed them, so they said to him, 'Go back to him.' So he went back to him, and he said to him, 'Did I not tell you, O cousin, drinking wine?' He went to them and informed them, so they said to him, 'Go back to him.' They did not cease with him until he went back to him and asked him. He said to him, 'Did I not tell you, O cousin, drinking wine?'

Indeed, drinking wine causes its drinker to enter into adultery, and theft, and the murder of the soul which Allah has prohibited, and into associating partners with Allah. And the effects of wine override every sin, just as its tree climbs over every tree.
ai.seo_question: What is the greatest major sin according to Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies drinking wine as the greatest major sin (*akbar al-kaba'ir*) during a dialogue with Quraysh in the Sacred Mosque. He elaborates that wine is the 'root' of all sins, leading to adultery, theft, and murder, using the metaphor of its tree overshadowing others to illustrate its pervasive corrupting influence. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on wine not merely as a standalone prohibition, but as the catalyst for a cascade of moral and spiritual decay.
